The power of the cuirass coursed throughout the chieftains body as he called forth the writhing and twisting vine, deftly manipulating it to open the sentinel's hatch and withdraw the creature within. AS it emerged, bound within the grip of the writhing tendril the Shaman was surprised to discover that the "Beast" the council was so concerned about was little more than a tired looking, blood-stained Med'ja "What is the meaning of this?" The Shaman asked, his patience now wearing thin "Do not be deceived by its appearance Shaman, it may wear the flesh of our kin but the strength and brutality of the beast surpasses even our fiercest warriors." "What is your name?" The Shaman asked, addressing the prisoner, who watched on silently with sunken eyes "I am Dew'ell, Son of Ad'jel, Brew master of the Med'ja-Hom'te" replied the captive with a toothy grin "The council believes you to be a monster, what say you?" The Brew master laughed at the Shaman's query, a harsh, wet cackle that made the hair on the Shaman's neck stand on end "A monster? no, I am not some mindless beast that hides in the shadows to steal its prey under cover of night. I am Med'ja! a proud son of Hom" "Lies!" The Chieftain spat, glowering with contempt. The captive began to cackle again at the Chieftain's outburst. "I do not lie to you Chieftain, I am indeed Dew'ell as I have always been, you should know better than anyone for was it not you who watched over my Denmates and I as we worked among the Mushrooms of our home? Was it not you who guided us through the tunnels of the Burrows? You know me Ma'te, Son of Tu'ras, no matter my sin."Then how!?" The Chieftian cried, his voice breaking "If you are indeed Dew'ell then how? how could you slaughter your own mate and Daughter?" "Oh Ma'te" the captive sighed "You would not understand. Life here among the vine was good and my work pleased the Gods but I am not the man I was" A rippled passed across the face of the Brew master, his features changing to mimic those of the Chieftain "My flesh, my form, is now as supple and malleable as the finest hide, i know not how this came to be but with it came a powerful hunger and an even greater thirst. At first I tried to resist at first, to ignore the calling within, it almost drove me to madness. You should have seen the look on their faces Ma'te, the taste of their blood, the sweetness of their flesh... richer than any Saen fruit. That is why they caught me, I could not resist adding such a flavor to my brew. It would have been exquisite. "You... Monster!" the Chieftain roared, his body trembling as power coursed through his body and the vine's grasp began to tighen, causing their captive to gasp as his features returned to normal "Chieftain! Compose yourself" The Shaman snapped, breaking him from his rage "This creature, this flesh changer seeks only to torment and goad you into folly, do not give in to its antagonism" "Yes" the Chieftain replied , his fury staved "Thank you Shaman" "What a horrible creature" remarked Sohti'le, The Cult of Umbralocht's representative among the council of Elders "What sort of God would birth such a beast" "That dear sister" Thad'ja responded "Is what I intend to uncover". Approaching the captive the Shaman grasped his staff tightly and placed the tip upon the Med'ja's forhead "What do you intend to do Shaman?" The brew master asked mockingly "I have no illness that needs curing, no ailment that requires rememdy, you are powerless" "Silence creature!" The Shaman barked "By the power contained with in this staff the secrets of your design shall be revealed. Such is the will of Hom" At the Shamans word a torrent of knowledge passed through his mind; Scenes of Gods in conflict, of a race cursed to consume those that unknowingly give refuge and of great flesh beasts writhing in the deep. "By The Gods..." The Shaman uttered, his staff clattering to the ground as he staggered back, the knowledge of the creatures origins striking a heavy blow upon his psyche. Taking the Shaman by the shoulders Lo'te, sister of Ma'te and partner to the throne, held the Shaman upright and turned him to face her "Are you alright Shaman? What did you see?" "This creature" The Shaman replied, pushing himself free of the Chieftain's hold "Is no lone beast, nor is it the work of some Shaman or Sorcerer. What stands before us is a child of Umbralocht himself, a Fleshchanged; creatures born to seek out the races of the world and to mimic those who reside where it can first gain refuge, destined to live exemplary lives until a time of great peace when they are forced to consume their kin. "Truely horrible" whispered Sohti'le, staring at the creature in awe "And yet our Masters most favored creation" "So what does it mean?" Ma'te asked, scowling at his compatriots admiration of her masters work "It means" Songcatcher replied "That the brew master could not control himself, no matter the severity of his crimes" "And yet he revels in the carnage of his deeds" "Such is the nature of their curse, he shall forever bear the desire to consume us and shall see no wrong in doing so" "Then there is no other choice" the chieftain sighed "He must be put to death" "Ma'te surely you are mad" the creature laughed "To believe such fanciful lies from a Shaman when the life of your own kin hangs in the balance" "No" said the Chieftain, shaking his head sadly "You are not my kin, you never were" With a deep breath, Ma'te, son of Tu'ras turned to face the tent's exit and addressed the Shaman and his council "I thank you all for joining me here this night but now I would ask that you retire to the council chambers and await my arrival, there is dark work yet to be done this night and I would not have you bear witness. Shaman, if you would be so kind I would like you to accompany the council and join them in the chambers. Thad'ja Songcatcher stood for a moment, inspecting the Chieftains back as if a secret was held within."As you wish" With a sigh he retrieved his staff and bowed to the Chieftain before exiting the tent. Lo'te approached her brother as the members of the council began to exit the tent one by one, placing a hand upon his shoulder "Brother are you certain of this?" "Yes sister" The Chieftain replied with a sigh "It must be this way, for safety and future of our tribe" For a moment the two Chieftains stood silent, eyes locked, a hidden conversation occurring within until at last, with a sad nod of acceptance, Lo'te turned to leave and accompany her kin.

For several hours the council and the Shaman sat in silence until just before dawn the Chieftain returned, his eyes ringed red and raw, his appearance haggard and gaunt. Slumping into his chair, he sat for what seemed like an eternity, his eyes closed as if sleeping or in prayer until at last they opened and the Chieftain spoke, his voice dry and hoarse "Do not lie to me Shaman, how many more of their kind dwell among us?" "It is impossible to say my lord for the nature of their birth is secret even to themselves. Only their reflection betrays them" Nodding, the Chieftain rested his forehead upon tented fingers and spoke, his words passing with a sigh "Then we will send word to the roost for mirrors of the highest quality, we have no other choice.
